newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain in shock over acquittal of cop killer.
newsitem.headline: Spain in shock over acquittal of cop killer.

text.p: The acquittal of a man who shot dead two Basque police officers shocked Spanish officials and many Basques and prompted calls on Friday for a ban on juries in cases where intimidation was possible.
Basque officials and judges said they suspected jurors had acquitted Mikel Otegi, an alleged member of radical youth group Jarria with links to ETA separatist guerrillas, for fear of reprisals.
"This is a true outrage that can only be attributed to fear," said Inaki Anasagasti, spokesman for the Basque National Party which heads the regional government.

A jury of eight women and one man acquitted Otegi on grounds he was not responsible for his actions when he killed two officers with a shotgun at a farm in Itsasondo in northern Spain in 1995, a San Sebastian court said late on Thursday.
Otegi, 23, had confessed to the killings but said in his defence that he had suffered a mental blackout at the time.
The Spanish state prosecutor made clear he would press for the verdict to be reconsidered.
"In the light of the alarm that this verdict has provoked, the state prosecutor's office will pursue all the legal recourses available," state prosecutor Juan Ortiz Urculo told reporters.

The case had been surrounded by controversy from the start due to difficulties in finding jurors for fear of retribution by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom). The court said the jurors had requested their names be expunged from the records.
The verdict raised doubts about the use of juries, a relatively new concept in Spain introduced in 1995.

"This is not a viable instrument at this time," Basque Interior Minister Juan Maria Atutxa said. "The climate here in the Basque region as in the Navarre region makes it impossible for a jury to be effective."
Political parties called for reform of the penal system and the government agreed changes were vital to avoid similar outcomes.
"It is very clear that such risky experiments will give the results we have here...The most important thing is that this type of situation is not repeated," said Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja.
The Basque region has suffered a climate of tension and fear due to ETA violence in the past 29 years. ETA has killed some 800 people in its fight for an independent Basque state.
Some Basque police officers expressed outrage at the sentence. "They have given a licence to kill whom they want," said one.
Many Basque citizens were also stunned."Our justice system is a complete joke and this proves it," a Basque shop owner said.
